findings.checklist_item: Specify how the file-path-qualified baseline keys for _compact_locked and rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log are relocated to their new module paths (or prove the post-decomposition CCN drops below the C901 scan threshold so no new key is emitted), so `--check` can report new=0 as the AC requires.
evidence: .github/complexity-baseline.json:7-9 has THREE compact.py entries: _compact_locked:24, compact_all_cli:17, rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log:21 — keyed by file path
scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py compare() lines 384-386: `if key not in baseline: counters.new.append(key)`; --check exits nonzero iff new>0 (docstring line 63)

Plan text: 'entries for _compact_locked and rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log are <= their current values (24/21) or removed entirely' — 'removed entirely' only avoids new>0 if the moved function drops below the scan threshold, which the plan does not establish
findings.finding: The plan's baseline-update strategy ('downward only', entries '<= current values (24/21) or removed entirely', check reports new=0) rests on an unverified premise: the complexity-baseline keys are FILE-PATH-qualified (`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py::_compact_locked`), and moving _compact_locked to compact_txn.py and rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log to compact_rebuild.py RENAMES those keys. check_complexity_baseline.py --check classifies any scanned key absent from the baseline as `new` (compare(), line 385-386) and exits nonzero when new>0. If either function still exceeds the C901 threshold after the planned decomposition, the scanner emits a NEW path-qualified key that the 'downward only / removed entirely' edit cannot satisfy — new>0, failing the AC. The plan neither relocates the keys to the new paths nor demonstrates the post-split CCN falls below the scan threshold.
findings.location: Approach ('Update .github/complexity-baseline.json downward only') and Acceptance Criteria line 2 (new=0 increased=0)
scenarios: After the split, _compact_locked still scores above the C901 threshold under its new path compact_txn.py::_compact_locked; the checker reports new=1, the gate fails, and the AC 'new=0' is unmet despite a 'downward-only' baseline edit

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the dependency-graph rationale to cover the compact_rebuild -> fsck_repair -> compact facade edge (rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log calls fsck_repair.rebuild_source_state), and specify that compact_rebuild imports fsck_repair in-body (mirroring fsck_repair's in-body compact import) so no top-level cycle forms.
evidence: compact.py:475 `compiled_state = fsck_repair.rebuild_source_state(ticket_id, ticket_dir)` — the rebuild engine depends on fsck_repair
fsck_repair.py:269 `from rebar._commands.compact import rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` (in-body) — fsck_repair depends back on the compact facade
compact.py:27 `from rebar._commands import _seam, fsck_repair` (module top) — compact imports fsck_repair eagerly
Plan quote: 'gives compact -> {txn, rebuild} and rebuild -> txn, which is acyclic' — the compact_rebuild->fsck_repair->compact edge is not accounted for
findings.finding: The plan's dependency-graph acyclicity analysis omits the compact_rebuild -> fsck_repair -> compact edge. rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log calls fsck_repair.rebuild_source_state (compact.py:475), and fsck_repair reaches rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log via an in-body import from rebar._commands.compact (fsck_repair.py:269), while compact.py imports fsck_repair at module TOP (line 27). The plan states the graph is 'compact -> {txn, rebuild}, rebuild -> txn ... acyclic' but never names where compact_rebuild imports fsck_repair; a top-level `from rebar._commands import fsck_repair` in compact_rebuild would form a real cycle if fsck_repair's compact import were ever hoisted, and even today the omission leaves the safety of the edge unstated.
findings.location: Approach section: 'Why the shared helpers live in compact_txn, not compact_rebuild' / dependency-graph claim
scenarios: compact_rebuild adds a top-level `from rebar._commands import fsck_repair` and fsck_repair's compact import is later moved to module scope, producing an import cycle
A reviewer/implementer trusts the stated acyclic graph and does not realize rebuild pulls in fsck_repair (which pulls the compact facade)
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'compact_rebuild also depends on fsck_repair.rebuild_source_state; import fsck_repair inside rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log (not at module top), mirroring fsck_repair.py:269 which imports the compact facade in-body — so the compact_rebuild<->fsck_repair pair stays acyclic at import time.'

findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC bullet: `python -c` (or a unit test) that captures get_rebuild_count(), invokes a rebuild against a fixture, and asserts the count incremented by 1.
